_comment: Rules for tools/licence-scan.py. Every list stays short and every exemption gives its reason (the scanner refuses to load one without). The allow-list is this fork's licence policy: widening it, or recording a new permission, is a maintainer decision, not a contributor's.
_allow: CC-BY-4.0 covers art and presets only (textures, models, sounds, structures, world presets), never code. SunPro is Sun's fdlibm notice ('Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software is freely granted, provided that this notice is preserved'), a permissive notice.

wording.why: GNU GPL, LGPL or AGPL licence text: copyleft, not on the allow-list
GNU LGPL licence text: copyleft, not on the allow-list
GNU AGPL: network copyleft, not on the allow-list
the Free Software Foundation, named by GPL-family headers
a licence identifier that is not on the allow-list
'All rights reserved' in a header: no permission to copy
a Stack Exchange answer: CC BY-SA, not on the allow-list for code

provenance.why: glibc is LGPL-2.1: its code may not be copied or ported
the IBM 'Ultimate Solution' routines in glibc, LGPL-2.1

exempt.why: the scanner names the rules it enforces
the register names each third-party licence
states what the fork's licence covers and on what permission the original code is used

reproduces fdlibm's SunPro notice, which it must preserve (it says 'All rights reserved' before granting permission), and explains that C libraries use the same formulas; its THIRD_PARTY.md row is SunPro

jar_licences._comment: group:artifact -> licence, for a bundled library whose own POM names none; each row says where the licence was read. The worlds' jars bundle no libraries today.

permissions._comment: Code used by its author's permission with no open-source licence. A register row says `PERMISSION <name>`; each name says where the permission is recorded. Adding one is a maintainer decision.

cbscript.record: NOTICE.md: used with the author's written permission, held by the maintainer

python_licences._comment: package -> licence, for the Python packages requirements.txt asks a user to install; each row says where the licence was read.

ply.source: PLY 3.11 by David M. Beazley: its README and the notice at the top of every ply/*.py file name the BSD 3-clause licence

pyyaml.source: PyYAML's LICENSE (github.com/yaml/pyyaml) and its PyPI metadata
